title: Real Madrid 2-1 Celta Vigo: Super sub Espi nets winner again for Mourinho's side
subtitle: Just as he did against Espanyol and Elche earlier in the season, Carlos Espi proved to be the matchwinner for Real Madrid in LaLiga.
paragraphs: Carlos Espi scored an 85th-minute winner as Real Madrid came from behind to defeat Celta Vigo 2-1 in LaLiga.

Pablo Duran gave Celta a shock lead at the Estadio Bernabeu, but second-half goals from Jude Bellingham and Carlos Espi, which came after Kylian Mbappe missed a penalty, clinched all three points for Jose Mourinho's side.
Celta stunned the home fans after just six minutes, with Duran tapping in from inside the six-yard box after being picked out by Williot Swedberg's drilled cross from the left side of the area.

Bernardo Silva went close to an equaliser, though he headed wide from Yan Diomande's delivery, while Swedberg missed two chances to double Celta's lead, first firing into the side netting from a cut-back before being thwarted by Thibaut Courtois.
Then came Mbappe's penalty miss in the 39th minute; after he was brought down in the box by Javi Rodriguez, the Frenchman strolled up to the spot before sending his strike well over the crossbar.

Mourinho introduced Marc Cucurella, Vinicius Junior and Federico Valverde in a triple substitution just before the hour, but Celta still looked the more threatening, with Ferran Jutgla skewing narrowly wide before Duran was kept out at full stretch by Courtois.

And just 35 seconds after Courtois denied Duran, Bellingham equalised for Madrid. Vinicius and Mbappe combined in the box before the latter teed up Bellingham, who flashed a strike into the bottom-left corner.

Los Blancos completed the turnaround with five minutes to go as Bellingham drove forward before laying off to Vinicius, whose cross was finished off by Espi on the second attempt, after his initial header was saved by Ionut Radu.

Madrid always looked like scoring the winner after Bellingham's equaliser in the 66th minute, but they had to rely on late heroics once again from Espi to get over the line and move level on points with leaders Barcelona.
The 21-year-old has now scored late winners off the bench against Espanyol, Elche and Celta this season, while he also netted in Madrid's stunning comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League.
Espi has scored more goals as a substitute than any other player in Europe's top-five leagues this season across all competitions, netting four times from just six shots on target.

Los Blancos dominated the expected goals (xG) tally, accumulating 3.76 from 24 shots to Celta's 1.64 from eight attempts, and Mbappe was given a reprieve for his penalty miss; he has missed six of the 28 penalties he has taken for Madrid across all competitions (excluding shoot-outs).

Bellingham made another vital contribution on what was his 100th LaLiga appearance, which he marked with his 39th goal in the competition. He is just the third Englishman to reach that milestone, after David Beckham (116 appearances) and Gary Lineker (103).
